newsitem.title: INDIA: India, South Africa launch "strategic partnership".
newsitem.headline: India, South Africa launch "strategic partnership".

text.p: India and South Africa on Friday launched a strategic partnership, seeking economic cooperation in shared Indian Ocean waters and democratic reforms in the United Nations for equal powers to all nations.

Visiting South African President Nelson Mandela and Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda signed the declaration at Delhi's 17th-century Red Fort during a reception in honour of Mandela, who was on the second day of a three-day visit.

"Convinced that the United Nations structures needed to be more representative of the concerns and diversities of the developing world, India and South Africa re-emphasise their belief in the need for U.N. reforms," United News of India (UNI) quoted the declaration as saying.

"We are in favour of a drastic restructuring of the (United Nations) Security Council," Mandela told a news conference earlier on Friday. He said U.N. members should have equal powers and not be restrained by vetoes enjoyed by a few.

The joint declaration expressed the resolve of the two nations to coordinate effors to make the recently formed Indian Ocean Rim Association for Regional Cooperation (IORARC) "an instrument of subsantive partnership", the Press Trust of India said.
The two nations have been leading efforts to form the basis for a free-trade bloc of Indian Ocean Rim countries.

"The economies of India and South Africa have certain comparative advantages, complementarities and resources which can be optimally used to promote economic development thorugh cooperation," the declaration said.
It said the two countries recognised South Africa's geo-strategic location as a trans-shipment point between Asia, Africa and Latin America.
Mandela said he expected India to support South Africa's bid to host the Olympic Games in Cape Town in 2004.
"I have no doubt that if we make a bid, whether we ask India or not, they will support us," he said.

South Africa would be equally keen to consider in a similar vein India's efforts for a permanent seat in the United Nations' Security Council in view of New Delhi's constant support to his African National Congress in its struggle against the apartheid policies of racial segregation, Mandela said.

"I have no doubts that if India wants a permanent seat in the U.N. Security Council, this is a matter that will be examined by South Africa from the point of view of the enormous and extensive support they have given to our struggle," Mandela said.
